fossil
The papersThe code

Overestimation in meta-analysis, dug back up.

The authors' simulation code was never released. We rebuilt it from the paper and its appendices as the Python package oisim and reran all 36 scenarios, 20,000 meta-analyses of 100 trials each. Of 91 results, 0 are exact, 13 agree, 20 partly agree, 38 are inconclusive, 16 differ and 4 were not attempted. The main claim holds on our run.

The formula is right: the unrounded OIS is within one rounding step of 140 of the 144 printed cells. The rounding is not the one the footnote states (78 of 144 cells) nor any single rule; the best rule we found gives 123 of 144 (62 patients, 61 events). Of the PC 10% patient cells, those for RRR 30% with I2 0% are printed to the nearest 100 and the rest to the nearest 500.

Table 1 (Cochrane trial sizes, PC 1-5% and 5-15%: patients and events required)Partly agrees81 of 144 values as printed81 of 144 cells as printed, 135 within one bin (500 patients or 50 events), 140 within two. Our two runs with different seeds agree with each other on 87 of 144 cells, so most of the misses are the size of chance; where ours misses, it is higher 51 times and lower 12 times, which chance alone would not give.
Table S3 ('common' trial sizes, PC 15-40% and 40-80%)Partly agrees71 of 144 values as printed71 of 144 cells as printed, 123 within one bin (100 patients or 50 events). Our two runs agree with each other on 85 of 144. Ours is higher 47 times and lower 26 times; with true RRR 10% and PC 15-40% the paper needs more patients than we do.
Table S4 ('common' trial sizes, PC 1-5% and 5-15%)Partly agrees101 of 144 values as printed101 of 144 cells as printed, 138 within one bin (500 patients or 50 events). Our two runs agree with each other on 124 of 144. Ours is higher 28 times and lower 15 times, mostly in the patients of PC 1-5%.
Table 2 (72 optimal information sizes, patients and events)Partly agrees123 of 144 values as printedThe formula is right: the unrounded OIS is within one rounding step of 140 of the 144 printed cells. The rounding is not the one the footnote states (78 of 144 cells) nor any single rule; the best rule we found gives 123 of 144 (62 patients, 61 events). Of the PC 10% patient cells, those for RRR 30% with I2 0% are printed to the nearest 100 and the rest to the nearest 500.
Table 3, OIS columns (ranges over I2 from Table 2)Partly agrees15 of 24 values as printed15 of 24 ranges as printed; every other range has both ends within one rounding step (1,000 patients, 50 events) of ours (9 of 9): the paper re-rounds Table 2's ends (9,600-19,500 is printed 10000-20000). Table 3 also prints PC '3%' for the 5-15% row, whose values are the 10% OIS.
Table 3, simulation columns (acceptability ranges, Cochrane trial sizes)Not attemptednot attemptedThe paper does not say how the ranges were formed ('post hoc'), and no rule we tried rebuilds them from the paper's own Tables 1, S3 and S4: of 54 range rules (threshold, true effect, levels; minimum to maximum over tau2) the best gives 8 of the 72 cells of Tables 3 and 4, and the Methods' own definitions of good, very good and excellent give at most 8. Without a rule that works on the paper's numbers, ours cannot be compared.
Table 4, OIS columnsPartly agrees31 of 48 values as printed31 of 48 ranges as printed; every other range has both ends within one rounding step of ours (17 of 17). Table 4 prints the PC 3% patient ranges as '10–20000' (10,000 to 20,000), and its caption repeats Table 3's ('Cochrane Heart Group') although its rows are the 'common' sizes of Tables S3 and S4.
Table 4, simulation columns (acceptability ranges, 'common' trial sizes)Not attemptednot attemptedAs for Table 3: no range rule we tried rebuilds these columns from the paper's own Tables S3 and S4 (best 8 of 72 cells over Tables 3 and 4; the Methods' definitions at most 8).
Table S1, Table S2 and Fig. S13 (survey of Cochrane Heart Group meta-analyses)Not attemptednot attemptedA survey of the 2009 Cochrane Heart Group mortality meta-analyses that set the simulation's inputs. The reviews are not listed (Table S1 numbers 20 of the '23' the text names), so the survey cannot be redone. Table S2's 'proportions used for simulations' are an input of our simulation, not a result.
Text: the larger the overestimation, the fewer patients and events requiredAgrees1 of 1 values as printed
  • >30% needs no more than >20% (all three tables): paper yes, ours yes
Text: low control risk needs more patients but fewer eventsAgrees2 of 2 values as printed
  • PC 1-5% needs more patients than 5-15% (Tables 1, S4): paper yes, ours yes
  • PC 1-5% needs fewer events than 5-15% (Tables 1, S4): paper yes, ours yes
Text: tau2 0.05 needs fewer than 0.25, reversed for 'common' sizes with PC 1-5%Agrees2 of 2 values as printed
  • tau2 0.05 needs fewer than 0.25 (except common sizes, PC 1-5%): paper yes, ours yes
  • common sizes, PC 1-5%: tau2 0.05 needs more than 0.25: paper yes, ours yes
Text (main claim): surpassing the OIS generally protects against overestimationAgrees1 of 1 values as printed
  • P(RRR > T) below 5% at or before the OIS for RRR = T, 90% power: paper yes, ours yes
Text: the probability of overestimation was above 25% when patients were few, in most scenariosAgrees1 of 1 values as printed
  • first point of the RRR > 20% patient curve above 25% (36 scenarios): paper yes, ours yes
Text claims recomputed from the paper's own tablesAgrees6 of 6 statements follow from the paper's own Tables 1, S3, S4 and 2: text.larger_overestimation (>30% needs no more than >20% (all three tables)): yes, 100% of cases; text.control_risk (PC 1-5% needs more patients than 5-15% (Tables 1, S4)): yes, 100% of cases; text.control_risk (PC 1-5% needs fewer events than 5-15% (Tables 1, S4)): yes, 89% of cases; text.heterogeneity (tau2 0.05 needs fewer than 0.25 (except common sizes, PC 1-5%)): yes, 92% of cases; text.heterogeneity (common sizes, PC 1-5%: tau2 0.05 needs more than 0.25): yes, 100% of cases; text.ois_protects (P(RRR > T) below 5% at or before the OIS for RRR = T, 90% power): yes, 76% of cases. The claim about early probabilities above 25% rests on the figures only.
Python package oisim and its tutorialAgreesoisim 0.1.0: wheel installed in a fresh environment and imported from it; tests 6 passed; tutorial 7 cells compared, 0 skipped (nondeterministic); TUTORIAL.md in sync

The main finding of the paper holds: on our run, surpassing the optimal information size protects against overestimation in most scenarios, as it does on the paper's own tables. The read-off tables agree within one bin for most cells; the remaining differences, and the offsets between our curves and the published ones, are open.

What came back

The method
DerSimonian-Laird cumulative meta-analysis and the trial generator of Appendices S1 and S2, as the package oisim.
Table 2
The OIS formula. 140 of 144 printed cells are within one rounding step of it; 123 match the best rounding rule we found.
Tables 1, S3, S4
81, 71 and 101 of 144 cells as printed; 135, 123 and 138 within one bin.
The claims
All four statements about the tables hold on our run and on the paper's own tables; the fifth, read from the figures, holds on our run.

What stayed buried

  • How the paper binned the curves and read the tables off them. We searched; the tables fit one rule and the figures another.
  • How Tables 3 and 4 group the scenarios into ranges. No rule we tried rebuilds them from the paper's own tables.
  • The survey of Cochrane Heart Group reviews behind Tables S1 and S2. The reviews are not listed.

The main finding of the paper holds: on our run, surpassing the optimal information size protects against overestimation in most scenarios, as it does on the paper's own tables. The read-off tables agree within one bin for most cells; the remaining differences, and the offsets between our curves and the published ones, are open.

What we matched

Each figure panel is scored both ways on the published pixel grid, against wrong inputs, near misses and our own second run. Each table cell is compared as printed.

Figure panels
74 panels: 6 agree, 14 partly, 38 inconclusive, 16 differ.
Table cells
144 + 144 + 144 read-off cells, 144 OIS cells, 72 OIS ranges.
Our two runs
Agree with each other on 87, 85 and 124 of 144 cells of Tables 1, S3 and S4.

The simulation was rebuilt in November 2026. The tables agree within one bin for most cells and the claims hold; the curves do not match exactly.
